ex: Open this link in your web browser, please.
Which browser do you use on your phone?
My browser is slow, so I need to update it.
You can save this page in your browser.
A string quartet played music at our wedding.
The quartet has two violins, a viola, and a cello.
She sings in a small jazz quartet on weekends.
Tickets for the quartet's concert cost twenty dollars.
A photon is a tiny particle of light.
The laser sends out one photon at a time.
Photons have no mass and move very fast.
In physics class, we learned what a photon is.
She wrote her school essay on feminism.
Feminism fights for equal rights for women.
This book is a classic of modern feminism.
We talked about feminism in our history class.
This movie is a classic example of noir.
In noir, a detective often walks through rainy streets.
She likes crime novels, especially dark noir.
Do you prefer comedy or noir for movie night?
There are clear parallels between these two stories.
Kyiv is just north of the 50th parallel.
Can you see any parallels between the two cases?
The teacher drew a parallel between the two wars.
parallel.note: Most often "parallel" is an adjective: "Draw two parallel lines."

ex: She cooked tofu with rice and vegetables.
Tofu is made from soybeans and water.
I'd like the spicy tofu soup, please.
Can you buy some tofu at the store?
tofu.note: Uncountable: some tofu, a piece of tofu (not "a tofu").

quartz.note: Uncountable: a piece of quartz (not "a quartz").

ex: An anarchist believes we do not need any government.
A group of anarchists protested outside the bank.
He read many books by famous anarchists.
She was an anarchist when she was young.
She won a free phone in an online giveaway.
The new store has a giveaway for its first customers.
How do I join the giveaway on your page?
The winner of our giveaway gets two concert tickets.
giveaway.note: Also a clue that shows a secret: "His smile was a dead giveaway."

ex: Cigarettes contain nicotine, which is bad for you.
Nicotine is very addictive, so quitting is hard.
He chews nicotine gum to stop smoking.
Does this vape have any nicotine in it?
nicotine.note: Uncountable: a lot of nicotine (not "a nicotine").

shooter.note: Most often "shooter" means a person who shoots a gun: "Police caught the shooter."

brief.note: Most often "brief" is an adjective meaning short: "a brief meeting."

groove.note: Most often "groove" means a long, narrow cut in a surface: "a groove in the wood."

ex: In old England, a yeoman owned and farmed his own land.
A yeoman was richer than a poor farm worker.
Many yeomen lived in the villages near the castle.
The museum has a room about the life of a yeoman.
yeoman.note: Also in "yeoman's work": hard, useful work.

MC.note: Short for "master of ceremonies"; in hip-hop, an MC is a rapper.

ex: The nurse placed electrodes on my chest.
Every battery has two electrodes inside it.
The electrode sends a small electric current.
Please clean the electrodes before you use them.
In the old story, the servant called him sahib.
The old sahib lived in a big white house.
"Yes, sahib," said the driver, and opened the door.
The sahib gave orders to the workers every morning.

developer.note: Most often "developer" means a software developer: "She is a web developer."

ex: Ciao, see you tomorrow at work!
She waved at us and said, "Ciao!"
Okay, I have to go now. Ciao!
He always says ciao instead of goodbye.
ciao.note: Informal; "bye" or "see you" are more common in English.

ex: Her ring has a small blue sapphire.
Sapphires are very hard and expensive stones.
He gave her sapphire earrings for her birthday.
How much does this sapphire necklace cost?
The farmers in our village formed a cooperative.
She buys fresh food at a local cooperative.
The cooperative is owned by all its members.
He lives in an apartment in a housing cooperative.
cooperative.note: Most often "cooperative" is an adjective meaning helpful: "The staff were very cooperative."

ex: The travelers stopped at an oasis in the desert.
An oasis has water and palm trees.
This small park is a green oasis in the city.
The camels drank water at the oasis.
Cyanide is a very dangerous poison.
In the movie, the spy carried a cyanide pill.
Apple seeds contain a small amount of cyanide.
Tests found traces of cyanide in the river water.
cyanide.note: Uncountable: a small amount of cyanide (not "a cyanide").

ramen.note: Uncountable: a bowl of ramen (not "a ramen").

ex: I'd like a salmon roll and green tea, please.
These sushi rolls are fresh and a little spicy.
Can we order two more rolls for the table?
She makes sushi rolls with rice and fish at home.
roll.note: Most often "roll" is a verb: "The ball rolled under the table."

premier.note: Most often "premier" is an adjective meaning best or leading: "a premier hotel."

ex: Don't tell me the ending, that's a spoiler!
This review has spoilers, so be careful.
I stay off social media to avoid spoilers.
Is it a spoiler if I tell you who wins?

vegan.note: Most often "vegan" is an adjective: "vegan food," "a vegan restaurant."

ex: The Brahmin led the prayers at the temple.
His family belongs to the Brahmin caste.
A Brahmin read from the old holy books.
In the past, Brahmins were priests and teachers.
brahmin.note: Usually written with a capital letter: "Brahmin."

brandy cola.note: In English, usually "brandy and Coke" or "brandy and cola."
